response: {"turns":[{"id":"M1:T21","text":"Okay."},{"id":"M1:T22","text":"Yes, that makes sense."},{"id":"M1:T23","text":"And on top of that, the system has to be able to export the audit trail for specific cases, without touching the audit trail it keeps stored itself. That's something external auditors could use if they want to look into or analyse what's been happening in the system."},{"id":"M1:T24","text":"Got it."},{"id":"M1:T25","text":"Also, the audit trail has to be kept for as long as it's required,"},{"id":"M1:T26","text":"Right."},{"id":"M1:T27","text":"and that's at the very least for the whole life of the case it relates to."},{"id":"M1:T28","text":"Okay."},{"id":"M1:T29","text":"On reporting, at a minimum the system needs to give us reports of actions on cases organised three ways: by case, by user, and in chronological order."},{"id":"M1:T30","text":"Sure."},{"id":"M1:T31","text":"Just to define it, an audit trail is a record of actions taken either by the user or by system triggers. So that covers what users or Administrators do, and also anything the system kicks off automatically because of system parameters. The system has to keep an unalterable audit trail that automatically captures and stores: every action, so create, read, update, delete, taken on the critical entities like case, suspect, property and so on; the user who initiated or carried out the action; the date and time of the event; and administrative parameters. And by unalterable I mean nobody can modify the audit trail data in any way or delete it. It can be re-departmented or copied to removable media if needed, as long as the contents stay unchanged."},{"id":"M1:T32","text":"Understood."},{"id":"M1:T33","text":"Okay, let's move on to the access module. How should access work?"},{"id":"M1:T34","text":"Changes to security attributes for groups or users, so access rights, security level, privileges, password allocation and management, those should only be made by the super-user."},{"id":"M1:T35","text":"Okay."},{"id":"M1:T36","text":"Then, if a user tries to access or search for a case they don't have the right to see, the system has to respond in one of three ways, and that's selectable at configuration time. One, show the title and metadata. Two, show that the case exists but not its title or any other metadata. Three, don't show any case information or hint that it exists at all. Those go in order of increasing security. And the third one, the strictest, means the system can't even count those cases in the search result totals. That level is normally what you'd want for cases about things like national security."},{"id":"M1:T37","text":"I see."},{"id":"M1:T38","text":"And related to that, if a user does a quick"},{"id":"M1:T39","text":"or an advanced search, the system must never put any record in the result list that the user doesn't have the right to access."},{"id":"M1:T40","text":"So whether it's a quick search or an advanced one, records the user isn't allowed to access should never show up in their result list, correct?"}]}
